boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fort Stedman record (March 25, 1865) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Hatcher's Run (VA083) precedes; the April operations belong to the Appomattox Campaign. The Union capture of the picket lines on March 25 is context for April 2, not this record's result. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Corps' and the live field zero; the frozen description says Lee amassed nearly half his army. Humphreys relays Gordon's statement that Lee gave him his own corps, parts of Hill's and Longstreet's and some cavalry, about one-half of the army, gives the Ninth Corps a seven-mile line, and gives the latest spring returns as not less than 46,000 effective Confederate infantry and 69,000 for the Army of the Potomac.
claims.rationale: A proportion, a line length and army-wide returns dated to late March; no count of the assaulting or defending force. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Humphreys says Hartranft retook Fort Stedman with small loss and that the Second and Sixth Corps took the Confederate picket lines; Lee says two efforts to recover the works were repulsed before his troops withdrew, and that at dark the enemy held much of the advanced line.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The picket-line captures are retained as context for April 2, a later record.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 3,850 (US 950; CS 2,900) and the live field 3,698 (US 1,017; CS 2,681). Humphreys gives Parke's 1,949 prisoners and loss of 494 killed and wounded and 523 missing (1,017), the Second Corps' 690 and 358 prisoners, the Sixth Corps' about 400 and 547 prisoners, and his estimate of nearly 4,000 Confederate and about 2,000 Union losses for the day; Lee reports 9 guns, 8 mortars and between 500 and 600 prisoners taken and his loss not heavy.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Parke's 1,017 matches the live Union figure, not the frozen 950; Humphreys' day totals include the picket-line fighting.

open_questions: Parke's, Hartranft's, Willcox's and McLaughlen's reports (Volume XLVI Nos. 134, 154), the artillery reports (Nos. 9-28), Meade's report (No. 5), Gordon's report (No. 181; read, not selected), the Union casualty return (No. 3, garbled) and the Confederate returns (No. 180) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
